symptom: On an MPR v1 project (Mendix below 10.18, contents in the .mpr) every write through the Go library's own path hung forever: codec.Store.SaveUnit, codec.Store.FlushUnits and modelsdk.Model.Flush never returned. Measured on a fresh Studio Pro-authored 9.24.30 app: SaveUnit of a changed DomainModels$DomainModel did not return within 15s. mxcli exec was unaffected, because the MDL executor writes through Writer.UpdateRawUnit, which is why none of the 9.24 doctype runs ever saw it
cause: WriteTransaction.WriteUnit reconciles the new bytes with the stored ones (canon.Reconcile, ADR-0008) before writing, and read the stored ones with reader.GetRawUnitBytes, i.e. through reader.db. The reader opens SQLite with SetMaxOpenConns(1), and the transaction the caller began already holds that one connection, so the read waited for it forever. On v2 the stored bytes come from mprcontents/ and the read never touched the pool, so every v2 test passed
file: `modelsdk/mpr/writer_core.go` (`WriteTransaction.WriteUnit` reads through `wt.tx`; `reconcileAgainst` takes the stored-bytes reader), `modelsdk/mpr/reader.go` (`rawUnitBytes(q rowQuerier, id)` behind `GetRawUnitBytes`)
insight: With a one-connection pool, any read through the pool while a transaction is open is a deadlock, not a race, and it only shows on the storage format whose reads touch the database. A v2-only test suite cannot see it: the test that catches it must open a real v1 file through NewWriter (so the pool is the real one) and run Begin/WriteUnit/Commit under a deadline, otherwise the hang takes the whole package down instead of failing one test. Revert proof: the deadline test and a SaveUnit probe on a 9.24 app both time out on the old code and return in under 0.1s on the fix; mx check passes on the written project
